fixture_name: Cloverleaf-to-urban interchange conversion — INT preliminary design (Wikimedia PD geometry)
subject: judge-baseline

justifications.substance: Shortened collector-distributor weave carrying a recorded 1,100 pcu/h design-year peak-hour volume is a substantive, stage-appropriate sideswipe/rear-end exposure concern at preliminary design for a cloverleaf-conversion interchange.
justifications.evidence_grounding: The pivotal claim rests on the verbatim EV-IN-015 quote covering junction-type suitability for traffic volume/movements, channelling of conflicting streams and lane balance/through-lane continuity, combined with recorded GA-drawing geometry and volume inputs; EV-IN-004 confirms the PIARC checklist provenance.
justifications.jurisdiction_correctness: PIARC-baseline semantics respected: raised purely as a safety_concern under the qualified int:preliminary-design prompts with no compliance assertion, and HSM Part C / IHSDM appear only as optional analytical aids, not as jurisdictional requirements.
justifications.recommendation_quality: Specific and sequenced — run the Appendix 1 §10.2 junction prompts now, quantify weaving adequacy via HSM crash-prediction models or IHSDM, then lengthen the CD road or add entry ramp metering if flagged — all actionable and viable at preliminary design.
justifications.vru_coverage: Not applicable to this motorised weaving section, but explicitly acknowledged: grade-separated shared-use paths remove VRU exposure, so the finding correctly scopes road users to vehicle occupants.

justifications.substance: Identifies a substantive preliminary-design gap: retained shared-use paths meet free-flowing ramp entries at uncontrolled crossings, directly conflicting with recorded objectives to improve pedestrian/cycle continuity — a real VRU hazard addressable at this design stage.
justifications.evidence_grounding: Pivotal claim is supported by verbatim quotes EV-IN-016 (adequate pedestrian/cyclist provision at junctions) and EV-IN-005 (all road users/thematic VRU audits), tied to recorded scheme objectives and layout facts with no invented content.
justifications.jurisdiction_correctness: Stays within PIARC international preliminary-design semantics, frames the checklist prompts as support for a categorically distinct safety_concern rather than a compliance finding, and keeps design-stage scope explicit.
justifications.recommendation_quality: Specific and viable: apply thematic VRU audit, use Walkability Checklist/CQSI to design controlled or grade-separated crossings at each path/ramp interface, and signalise named terminal crossings — actionable at preliminary design with feasible options.
justifications.vru_coverage: Pedestrians and cyclists are the explicit focus throughout — exposure, crossing control needs, and continuity impacts are fully considered, exceeding the acknowledgment threshold.
